text.text_excerpt: Tucked away in the courtyard of 520 Royal St, also known as the "Bruletour Courtyard", Café Cour is run by the folks at Carmo and provides a lovely selection of beverages and light eats in the heart of the French Quarter. It shares the address with the Historic New Orleans Collection's most recently opened museum space and serves as the Museum Café. They offer pastries, coffees and tea, lunch options, salads, sandwiches, biscuits that I have heard folks RAVE about. They also have options for vegan, vegetarian, pescatarian and the folks who avoid gluten. The gumbo I had recently was outstanding, and the piperade tart with a little side salad was the PERFECT lunch at a GREAT price, so much ...

This gem hidden in the courtyard of the newest Historic New Orleans Collection buildings on Royal street serves up some tasty and inexpensive treats. Café Cour, run by the owners of Carmo, features outdoor seating only. You order at the counter and eat in the courtyard or take it to go. You are greeted by friendly staff who will take the time to explain what they feature that day or items on the menu with which you may be unfamiliar. Sandwiches such as jamon Serrano with manchego cheese served on a Belgrade baguette and served with a side salad are flavorful, filling and fit the budget at $10 - (a rarity in the FQ). They also have An array of empanadas, usually a soup of the day, salads, ...

CARMO COMES TO ROYAL STREET The biggest buzz on Royal Street among the merchants has been praise for Carmo's new offering, Cafe Cour in the courtyard of 520 Royal. The quality of food is just as high as at the Julia location. I am a particular fan of the sandwich specials with fresh garden salad (see pic). COURTYARD SEATING Which in pretty weather, like the upcoming fall, is truly delightful and reminiscent of the old Royal Cafe which served this neighborhood so well for decades.
